text:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has sought development partnerships with German cities in agriculture, information and communications technology (ICT) and youth skills acquisition to boost economic growth in Abuja.
Wike made the call when the German Ambassador to Nigeria, Stefan Rössel, visited him in Abuja.
The minister said the FCT Administration was committed to transforming Abuja into a world-class capital capable of competing with global cities such as Berlin, Munich and Washington, D.C.
He said the administration was working to provide a secure and conducive environment for diplomatic missions, businesses and foreign investors.
Wike noted that Abuja had faced challenges in security and urban infrastructure before the current administration but said efforts were being made to improve the situation through enhanced security and road construction.
“Our vision is to see Abuja become one of the best cities in the world. With the mandate to change the narrative, security and the environment have improved, and road infrastructure is being actively delivered,” he said.
On the country’s economic situation, the minister defended the reforms introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, including proposals for decentralisation and state policing to address insecurity.
While acknowledging the economic hardships faced by Nigerians, Wike urged citizens to be patient, saying the reforms were intended to deliver long-term benefits.
“Leadership is about taking bold decisions for long-term benefit. Things may be harsh now for a short while, but in the long run, the people will reap the benefits,” he said.
Earlier, Rössel highlighted the longstanding diplomatic relations between Nigeria and Germany, which he said had spanned 66 years, expressing his country’s readiness to deepen bilateral cooperation.
The ambassador commended the ongoing physical development in Abuja and acknowledged the federal government’s economic reform agenda.
He said the reforms would require time to translate into jobs and improved welfare but assured Nigeria of Germany’s continued support.
“As a new ambassador, it is immediately visible that this country is on the move,” he said.
Rössel added that the German Embassy and European Union member states were interested in collaborating with the FCT Administration on urban planning, infrastructure development and city governance.
He reaffirmed Germany’s commitment to supporting Nigeria’s economic and security policy initiatives.
